readmeExcerpt:
# chrome-cdp

Let your AI agent see and interact with your **live Chrome session** — the tabs you already have open, your logged-in accounts, your current page state. No browser automation framework, no separate browser instance, no re-login.

Works out of the box with any Chrome installation. One toggle to enable, nothing else to install.

## Why this matters

Most browser automation tools launch a fresh, isolated browser. This one connects to the Chrome you're already running, so your agent can:

- Read pages you're logged into (Gmail, GitHub, internal tools, ...)
- Interact with tabs you're actively working in
- See the actual state of a page mid-workflow, not a clean reload

## Installation

### As a pi skill

```bash
pi install git:github.com/pasky/chrome-cdp-skill@v1.0.1
```

### For other agents (Amp, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)

Clone or copy the `skills/chrome-cdp/` directory wherever your agent loads skills or context from. The only runtime dependency is **Node.js 22+** — no npm install needed.

### Enable remote debugging in Chrome

Navigate to `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` and toggle the switch. That's it.

The CLI auto-detects Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Edge, and Vivaldi on macOS, Linux, and Windows. If your browser stores `DevToolsActivePort` in a non-standard location, set the `CDP_PORT_FILE` environment variable to the full path.

## Usage

```bash
scripts/cdp.mjs list                              # list open tabs
scripts/cdp.mjs shot   <target>                   # screenshot → runtime dir
scripts/cdp.mjs snap   <target>                   # accessibility tree (compact, semantic)
scripts/cdp.mjs html   <target> [".selector"]     # full HTML or scoped to CSS selector
scripts/cdp.mjs eval   <target> "expression"      # evaluate JS in page context
scripts/cdp.mjs nav    <target> https://...       # navigate and wait for load
scripts/cdp.mjs net    <target>                   # network resource timing
scripts/cdp.mjs click  <target> "selector"        # click element by CSS selector
scripts/cdp.mjs clickxy <target> <x> <y>          # click at CSS pixel coordinates
scripts/cdp.mjs type   <target> "text"            # type at focused element (works in cross-origin iframes)
scripts/cdp.mjs loadall <target> "selector"       # click "load more" until gone
scripts/cdp.mjs evalraw <target> <method> [json]  # raw CDP command passthrough
scripts/cdp.mjs open   [url]                      # open new tab (triggers Allow prompt)
scripts/cdp.mjs stop   [target]                   # stop daemon(s)
```

`<target>` is a unique prefix of the targetId shown by `list`.

## Why not chrome-devtools-mcp?

[chrome-devtools-mcp](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp) reconnects on every command, so Chrome's "Allow debugging" modal can re-appear repeatedly and target enumeration times out with many tabs open. `chrome-cdp` holds one persistent daemon per tab — the modal fires once, and it handles 100+ tabs reliably.

## How it works

Connects directly to Chrome's remote debugging WebSocket — no Puppeteer, no intermediary. On first access to a tab, a lightweight background daemon is spawned that holds the session open. Chrome's "Allow debugging" modal appears once per tab; subsequent commands reuse the daemon silently. Daemons auto-exit after 20 minutes of inactivity.

This approach is also why it handles 100+ open tabs reliably, where tools built on Puppeteer often time out during target enumeration.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Let your AI agent interact directly with your live Chrome session via CDP without requiring a fresh browser or re-login.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Chrome-CDP is an agent skill that connects directly to a user's already running Chrome browser via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). Unlike standard automation frameworks that spin up fresh, isolated browser instances, this tool allows AI agents to interact with active tabs where the user is already logged in. It bypasses bulky dependencies like Puppeteer, relying on a lightweight background daemon that keeps the WebSocket connection open. This architecture prevents Chrome's "Allow debugging" modal from repeatedly appearing on every command and allows the tool to reliably manage environments with hundreds of open tabs without timing out.
keyFeatures: Live session integration: Connects to the user's active Chrome session, inheriting all existing logins and cookies.
Lightweight architecture: Operates entirely via raw CDP over WebSockets without requiring massive automation frameworks like Puppeteer or Playwright.
Persistent tab daemons: Spawns a background process per tab to hold the session open, preventing repeated permission prompts and timeouts.
Cross-origin iframe support: Capable of typing and interacting with elements embedded inside complex, cross-origin iframes.
Accessibility tree extraction: Captures a semantic, compact snapshot of the DOM specifically optimized for language models to parse.
No npm installation required: Runs as a standalone skill using Node.js, making it trivially easy to integrate into various agent frameworks.
Automatic browser detection: Auto-detects remote debugging ports across Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Edge, and Vivaldi on all major OS platforms.

useCases.title: Authenticated data extraction
useCases.description: Agents can pull data from internal corporate tools, Gmail, or GitHub without the user needing to manually provide API keys or cookies.

useCases.title: Live workflow assistance
useCases.description: Users can ask their agent to interact with a page they are actively looking at, reading the current state mid-workflow rather than reloading.

useCases.title: Agentic web automation
useCases.description: Developers can use the tool to give agents like Claude Code the ability to navigate, click, and fill out forms on live web pages.

useCases.title: High-volume tab management
useCases.description: Users with hundreds of open tabs can use the CLI to quickly locate tabs, take screenshots, or execute JavaScript across them.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This tool is built for users of AI agents (like Amp, Claude Code, or Cursor) and developers who want to grant their models direct access to their active browsing context. It requires Node.js 22+.
